run.question:
Alertmanager alert RequestErrorRate (severity warning) is firing for service otel-demo/checkout since 2026-11-17T04:19:55Z.
Investigate why this alert is firing.

report.summary: The RequestErrorRate alert for checkout fires because about 20% of checkout's oteldemo.CheckoutService/PlaceOrder calls fail with gRPC status 13 INTERNAL and the exact status description "shipping quote failure: failed POST to email service: expected 200, got 400". In every sampled failing trace the failing call is checkout's client span "HTTP POST" under prepareOrderItemsAndShippingQuoteFromCart, and the span that received it is shipping's "/get-quote" server span; that shipping span lasts 38-469 microseconds and has no child quote call, whereas successful quotes last ~17.7 ms and go /get-quote -> shipping "POST quote" -> quote "POST /getquote" -> calculate-quote. The email service is not on the failing path and returns HTTP 200; payment, quote and cart report no failures, all otel-demo pods are Running/Ready with 0 restarts, no evictions/OOM/network policies were found, and all flagd fault flags are off. Rate arithmetic confirms the link: shipping /get-quote runs at 0.95/s while shipping "POST quote" and quote "POST /getquote" run at ~0.75/s, and the ~0.196/s gap matches checkout's 0.197/s HTTP POST error rate. Failing checkouts appear to carry an empty cart (failing traces contain no checkout ProductCatalog/Currency spans, and the three failing cart users I checked had no AddItem before their GetCart), so the supported hypothesis is that shipping /get-quote answers HTTP 400 for empty-item quote requests; that trigger is inferred, not directly observed. Frontend, frontend-proxy and load-generator show their own HTTP 500 error spans carrying the same checkout error, i.e. propagation. Because the span-metric series begins at 04:19:50, seconds before the alert's 04:19:55, no pre-incident baseline exists and no trend/latency claim is made.

claims.text: checkout's oteldemo.CheckoutService/PlaceOrder error-span rate was 0 at 04:19:50 and then 0.233-0.489 spans/s per 5-minute window against 0.670-0.948 spans/s with STATUS_CODE_UNSET, still 0.140/s at 04:59:50; the series' first sample is 04:19:50.

All 150 checkout error spans sampled between 04:23:43 and 04:24:34 carry otel.status_code=ERROR, rpc.grpc.status_code=13 and otel.status_description/exception.message "shipping quote failure: failed POST to email service: expected 200, got 400".

In trace fabf30c40bb674e79e93dd78836bb231 the checkout PlaceOrder error span's child prepareOrderItemsAndShippingQuoteFromCart contains an erroring checkout span "HTTP POST" (826 us) whose child is shipping's "/get-quote" server span (469 us); frontend "POST /api/checkout" (500), frontend-proxy "ingress"/"router frontend egress" (500) and load-generator "POST" (500) also error in the same trace.

Two further failing checkout traces (c7625da06fae49e86716ba65e8fc52fb and 9d5c52c3dab41237d99a0e54fafc59e6) show the same shape: erroring checkout "HTTP POST" whose only child is shipping "/get-quote" of 38 us and 45 us respectively, with no quote-service or product-catalog span under it.

A successful checkout trace (03463095c70f822db5e7f6c234f10d36) shows shipping "/get-quote" 17.75 ms -> shipping "POST quote" -> quote "POST /getquote" -> "{closure}" -> calculate-quote, plus email "POST /send_order_confirmation" with http.status_code 200, so the same call path succeeds when it is not rejected.

At 04:59:50 (15-minute rates) shipping "/get-quote" was 0.9498 spans/s, shipping "POST quote" 0.7535/s and quote "POST /getquote" 0.7590/s, while checkout "HTTP POST" STATUS_CODE_ERROR was 0.1974/s; the ~0.196/s difference is quote requests that shipping did not forward to the quote service and matches the checkout error rate.

The email service is processing order-confirmation calls normally: email "POST /send_order_confirmation" ran at 0.7532/s (15m) and 0.7756/s (30m), and sampled email server spans returned http.status_code 200 with send_email and sinatra.render_template children.

The quote service logs a continuous stream of "Calculated quote" lines (436 lines between 04:19 and 04:26) and its span operations are "POST /getquote", "{closure}" and "calculate-quote", so it is processing the quote requests that shipping forwards.

All 21 otel-demo pods are Running and Ready with 0 restarts (including checkout-5dccddf8bb-vh65b, shipping-75d58f5d84-kgmz9, quote-6b5877698d-x6v2f and email-59f69bc6cf-7wqqk), and every otel-demo deployment was created 2026-11-17T04:09:46Z with 1/1 ready replicas and generation 1 (flagd and load-generator generation 2).

Events across all namespaces show no eviction, OOMKilled, FailedScheduling/backoff or Unhealthy event for the otel-demo workloads; the only otel-demo change is the load-generator rollout at 04:44:01-04:44:02 (Deployment load-generator ScalingReplicaSet, ReplicaSet load-generator-7d5756fbd9 SuccessfulCreate/SuccessfulDelete of pod load-generator-c7cbc4c99-xlnk2).

ConfigMap flagd-config has all fault-injection flags (adFailure, adHighCpu, adManualGc, cartFailure, emailMemoryLeak, imageSlowLoad, kafkaQueueProblems, paymentFailure, paymentUnreachable, productCatalogFailure, recommendationCacheFailure) at defaultVariant "off"; only loadGeneratorFloodHomepage defaults to "100" ("Flood the frontend with a large amount of requests").

The cart-service records for three users whose checkouts failed show no cart population before their GetCart: userId 998af264 appears only as GetCartAsync at 04:24:19.463 in 04:23:50-04:25:10, userId 94da6574 appears only as GetCartAsync at 04:24:08.966 in 04:23:00-04:25:30, and userId 9f5f8f6a's GetCartAsync at 04:24:29.485 precedes its only AddItemAsync at 04:25:16.562.

Other services' error spans at 04:59:50 are either zero (payment, accounting) or small background rates (fraud-detection 0.00116/s, ad 0.00232/s, recommendation 0.00116/s), while the elevated rates are checkout 0.3948/s, frontend 0.7187/s and frontend-proxy 17.47/s error spans/s.

The HTTP 400 from shipping /get-quote is most likely its response to a quote request whose item list is empty: the failing traces contain no checkout ProductCatalog/GetProduct or CurrencyService/Convert spans (no items iterated), and the three failing cart users had no AddItem before their GetCart. This is inferred because request bodies are not observable and shipping logs only successful quotes.

The phrase "failed POST to email service" in checkout's error text does not match the traced call path: the failing POST is answered by shipping's /get-quote span, no email span exists in the failing traces, and email returns 200, so the wording looks like a code/labeling defect in checkout rather than the identity of the failing dependency.

The only non-off fault-injection setting, flagd loadGeneratorFloodHomepage defaultVariant "100", may raise frontend/load-generator traffic, but nothing in the evidence ties it to the empty-cart checkouts or to shipping's HTTP 400 responses, so it remains an unconfirmed candidate rather than this cause.

The quote service is not where the failures happen: failing requests contain no quote span, and quote "POST /getquote" (0.7590/s) matches shipping "POST quote" (0.7535/s), i.e. quote handles every request shipping forwards.
Payment is not failing in this window: payment's error-span rate was 0 at 04:59:50 and the successful checkout trace shows oteldemo.PaymentService/Charge with rpc.grpc.status_code 0.

Pod or node-level failure is not supported: all otel-demo pods are Running/Ready with restart count 0, events show no Evicted/OOMKilled/FailedScheduling/Unhealthy entries for demo workloads, and no NetworkPolicy objects were returned for the cluster (that query returned no data, so absence of network policies is not asserted).

The flagd fault flags were considered as the injected cause and rejected: paymentFailure, paymentUnreachable, cartFailure, adFailure, emailMemoryLeak, productCatalogFailure, recommendationCacheFailure, adHighCpu, adManualGc, imageSlowLoad and kafkaQueueProblems all have defaultVariant "off", and none of them declares an HTTP 400 from a shipping quote endpoint.

An email-service outage was considered and rejected as the cause: email spans show http.status_code 200, failing traces contain no email span, and the failing dependency span is shipping "/get-quote".

Review the shipping Deployment's /get-quote request validation and decide the intended behaviour for a quote request with no items (explicit 4xx contract vs successful empty quote), then align checkout so that an empty cart is rejected before the shipping call.

Fix the checkout error text returned on the shipping-quote HTTP failure (it names the email service although the traced call is shipping /get-quote) and return a distinguishable status for empty-cart checkouts so alerting is not driven by them.

Because the alert threshold is "above 0" and the span-metric series only begins at 04:19:50, add an explicit baseline/threshold and retain pre-incident series before tuning the RequestErrorRate rule for checkout.

gaps: No data before 04:19:50: the traces_span_metrics series for checkout PlaceOrder starts at 04:19:50 (four seconds before the alert's 04:19:55) and Prometheus started at 04:17:35, so whether the error rate increased, and what a pre-incident baseline was, cannot be established.

HTTP request bodies and the shipping service's exact 4xx validation rule are not observable; the empty-item-list trigger is inferred from missing GetProduct/Convert spans and cart-service logs, not from the request itself.
shipping logs only successful quotes and its /get-quote span records no error status, so the internal reason it returned HTTP 400 for those requests is unknown.
Kubernetes events are only retained from ~04:24:35 onward, so events for the 04:09-04:24 period (including any checkout/shipping rollout) are unavailable.
The change_history integration is not available, so no change or rollout history can be checked.
Secrets (such as any credentials or hidden configuration consumed by the services) cannot be read and were not verified.
next_steps: Inspect the shipping Deployment's /get-quote handler and its validation of an empty item list, and the checkout Deployment's shipping-quote error path and message text.

Check the load-generator's checkout journey and session/cart handling to see whether it deliberately issues PlaceOrder against empty carts, and whether the flagd loadGeneratorFloodHomepage flag is intended to be active.
Compare checkout PlaceOrder error ratio over a period with a real pre-incident baseline once longer metric retention is available.
